name: Jim Corbett National Park
examFacts: Oldest national park in India, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, later renamed Ramganga NP, and finally Corbett NP in 1957.
Birthplace of Project Tiger: launched here on 1 April 1973 by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
Ramganga River flows through the park, creating the iconic Patli Dun valley.
Possesses the highest tiger population density of any protected area in the world.
Dhikala tourism zone is the central grassland valley famous for herds of wild elephants and tigers.

name: Kaziranga National Park
examFacts: Hosts approximately two-thirds of the world's total surviving population of the Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros (~2,600+ rhinos).
Home to the 'Big Five' of Kaziranga: Rhinoceros, Royal Bengal Tiger, Asian Elephant, Wild Water Buffalo, and Eastern Swamp Deer.
Recognized as an Important Bird Area (IBA) by BirdLife International.
Situated on the southern floodplains of the Brahmaputra River, subject to annual monsoon inundation that replenishes nutrients.
Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985 and declared a Tiger Reserve in 2006.

name: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary
examFacts: Sole natural wild habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) in the entire world.
Saved from near-extinction by the conservation efforts of the Nawab of Junagadh, Muhammad Rasul Khanji, in the early 20th century when numbers dipped below 20.
Drained by seven perennial rivers: Hiran, Saraswati, Datardi, Shingoda, Machhundri, Raval, and Shetrunji.
Maldhari pastoralist nomadic community has coexisted inside Gir forests with lions for centuries.
The Supreme Court of India in 2013 ordered the translocation of a second population of Asiatic lions to Kuno Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh to prevent catastrophic epidemic extinction.

name: Sundarbans National Park
unescoStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987) & Ramsar Wetland (2019)
examFacts: World's only mangrove forest inhabited by tigers; Sundarbans tigers are uniquely adapted to swimming across broad tidal channels and drinking brackish water.
Named after the dominant mangrove tree species 'Sundari' (Heritiera fomes), noted for specialized pneumatophore roots (blind breathing roots).
Largest Ramsar Wetland site in India (4,230 sq km total Indian Sundarbans).
Forms the lower delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers across India and Bangladesh.
One of the original nine Project Tiger reserves declared in 1973.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
examFacts: World's only floating national park, located on the southern fringes of Loktak Lake.
Exclusive wild refuge of the critically endangered Eld's deer subspecies Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii - State Animal of Manipur).
Consists of floating biomass mats called Phumdis (up to 4–5 feet thick) that float during the wet season and rest on the lake bed during the dry winter.
Sangai deer has evolved specialized splayed hooves adapted to walking on the spongy, floating phumdis without sinking.
Threatened by the permanent high water levels maintained by the Ithai Barrage.

name: Hemis National Park
examFacts: Largest national park in India by total area (~4,400 sq km).
Globally celebrated as the 'Snow Leopard Capital of the World', harboring the highest density of snow leopards in any protected area.
Bounded by the Indus River to the north and covers the catchments of Markha, Rumbak, and Sumdah streams.
Contains the historic 17th-century Hemis Gompa (Drukpa Kagyu lineage), Ladakh's largest and wealthiest monastery.
Entirely situated above 3,300 meters altitude in the Trans-Himalayan cold desert.
